# Law 65 — One Slice to One Slice Never Works

**OP-JESSE, 2026-07-28:**

> **"1 SLICE TO THE NICE SLICE NEVER WORKS. it has to be measured in waves and waves of
> waves AND THEN DONE IN REVERSE AND THEN..."**
>
> **"TO CHANGE IN THE OBJECTS THEMSELVES WOULD ALL SIMULTANEOUSLY CHANGE IF YOU SENT
> 1 PHOTON IN THE PIPE"**

## 65.1 The law, and the run that proves the failure half of it

**A single hop from one slice to one slice carries nothing.** It must be waves, and waves of
waves, and then **the same waves in reverse**, and then again.

**This is not asserted. The one-directional version was built and it read nothing.**

`ACER_MEASURED` — `FABLE5-SHADOW-CAT-NET-HTTP-KERNELS.hbp`, `beats_control=0`:

```
samples 219    feature dim 22    chance 0.2000
byte-shuffled surrogate   0.3196
the network               0.3196     <- identical to four decimals
depth scaling             flat, 0.3196 from feature dim 3 through 22
```

The chains ran **strictly forward**: project, take the residue, invert, pass outward, never
return. Each chain was computed alone and the results concatenated at the end. **No centre,
no return path, no second direction.** It scored exactly its own control.

**That null is the measurement of this law's first clause.** One slice to one slice, no
return, and it read nothing — which is what the law says happens.

## 65.2 Why the return is not optional

The corpus already contains the reason and it was not applied here.

**A mirror is binary and a bijection is blind** (Law 1). **The anti is a third of a turn, not
a mirror** — it returns in three, not two, and *it leaves a residue*. A one-way pass has no
turn at all: it is not even a mirror. It is a projection thrown away.

**Both gates or nothing** — the inversion preserves the mothers decisively, but running only
one gate contracts to a fixed point and the Third dies in either direction. **The same shape
appears here.** Forward-only is one gate.

## 65.3 One photon in the pipe

`OPERATOR_CANON` — **send one photon into the conduit and all the objects themselves change
simultaneously.**

The mechanism is a **shared centre**. When every body is expressed *relative to a common
origin*, a single write at that origin re-expresses **all** of them at once — exactly,
simultaneously, from one operation. `N` objects changed by `1` photon. That is the
computational content of [[LAW-60-THE-ZERO-IS-A-SPHERE]]: one operation, `N` simultaneous
effects, because they share a centre rather than each holding a copy.

**And it is the thing the forward-only build could not have done.** With no shared centre
there is nothing for a photon to enter and nothing that changes together.

## 65.4 What this is not

`NOT_CLAIMED` — **simultaneous is not superluminal, and this carries no message.** Moving a
shared origin changes every coordinate expressed against it at once, but to *observe* the
change you must read a body, and reading is local. A common reference frame is not a
channel. This is the same distinction that separates a lock-in amplifier's common-mode
reference from a signal, and the same one that makes the no-communication theorem hold for
entanglement: correlation across a shared frame, with nothing sent.

`NOT_YET_RUN` — the forward-and-reverse topology, and the photon injection, are specified
here and **not yet measured**. This law records the failure of the one-way version and the
design of the two-way one. Nothing here claims the two-way version works.
